edges.notes: Historical CentOS Linux releases shipped Linux kernel packages for supported architectures as part of the distribution.
CentOS Linux on standard ports used glibc as the C library alongside the dynamic linker.
systemd was the default init and service manager on CentOS Linux 7+ releases per project documentation themes.
CentOS Linux services were expressed as systemd unit files and drop-ins on default systemd installs where applicable.
CentOS Linux userland binaries and shared libraries were ELF on typical Linux targets.
GCC toolchain packages participated in CentOS Linux development and RPM build flows.
GNU binutils participated in standard CentOS Linux RPM build and link flows.
g++-built packages linked GNU libstdc++ above glibc on typical CentOS Linux GNU/Linux flows.
Clang/LLVM packages could be installed from CentOS Linux repositories where offered.
Official centos:* OCI images were common glibc-based bases; Docker pulls and runs legacy images where still published.
CRI/containerd nodes ran CentOS Linux-based workload images pulled as OCI artifacts in historical deployments.
CentOS Linux was a common historical node OS choice for on-prem Kubernetes clusters seeking RHEL-compatible glibc userlands.
CentOS Linux bases were packaged as OCI image rootfs layers conforming to OCI image layout conventions.
Substitutable Linux distribution defaults for containers and servers (glibc/systemd vs musl/OpenRC field patterns).
